purpose: Researched Danbooru-tag axes for generating Aria's FACE at scale. Consumed by face_lab.py. Kept as data rather than code for the same reason tags.json is: the vocabulary is the thing being refined overnight, and it must be editable without touching the runner.

provenance.verification_status: MOST AXIS ENTRIES ARE UNVERIFIED ON THIS RIG. tags.json's rule is that an entry is earned only after the prose form was observed to DROP the trait on a real generation. The entries below are researched-plausible Danbooru tags, not measured ones -- this overnight run IS the measurement pass. Promote entries into tags.json with verified:true only after reading the image back.

why_identity_is_not_an_axis.observed: 2026-08-18. generated/aria_clean + aria_float (seed 4242) and generated/aria_stars + aria_anim (seed 20260817) were intended as the same character and came out as two different girls.
why_identity_is_not_an_axis.diff: Every identity-carrying tag differed at once: blue eyes vs purple eyes + star-shaped pupils; 'two side up, purple star hair ornament' vs neither; 'black bowtie' vs 'black turtleneck'; no headphones vs headphones. The seed differed too.
why_identity_is_not_an_axis.cause: In a booru model, identity is carried by a small set of high-weight tags near the FRONT of the prompt. Changing several of them together does not produce a variation of a character, it produces a different character that merely shares the low-information remainder ('white hair, short hair, labcoat').
why_identity_is_not_an_axis.consequence_for_this_file: IDENTITY IS A CONSTANT, NOT AN AXIS. face_lab.py prepends it verbatim to every prompt and offers no way to vary it per-image. Axes may only add expression, framing, lighting, effects and background. Do not add an eye-colour, hair-shape, or outfit axis below -- that is precisely the mistake that produced two Arias.
why_identity_is_not_an_axis.chosen_by: Ari, 2026-08-18, from the four preset images. Reference variant.

identity.note: FROZEN. Byte-identical to make_dataset.py's IDENTITY prefix so LoRA-trained and non-LoRA generations describe the same character, and matched against assistant/web/aria.jpg. Reordering these tags moves the face -- do not resort them, do not reword them, do not 'improve' them.

framing.note: Face work, where 'face' means a BUST SHOT, not a macro crop. Danbooru's 'portrait', 'close-up' and 'face focus' all denote a tight head shot that fills the frame -- they are deliberately absent from every framing below and are suppressed in the negative instead.

framing.avatar_locked_note: MEASURED TWICE, 2026-08-18, seed 4242. First pass (generated/aria_face_probe/) compared framings on ONE cheerful expression and picked 'portrait, head and shoulders'. That was wrong, and wrong in an instructive way: it was judged on a single expression, and across the real canon tier it produced extreme close-ups with the crown and chin cut off (see ariaface_canon_00027_, pouty#3). Second pass (generated/aria_face_probe2/) re-ran the exact failing prompt across wider framings: 'upper body' WITH 'close-up, portrait, face focus' in the negative keeps the whole head, headroom, shoulders and the bowtie while the face stays large. 'cowboy shot' goes too far -- the face shrinks and the model starts drawing a framed-picture border. LESSON: probe framing on a DIFFICULT expression, not a flattering one. NOT FIXED: 'straight-on' still does not reliably level the head.

axes.note: Sampled combinatorially by face_lab.py's deep tier. Booru models degrade past roughly 40 tags, so the sampler draws a SUBSET of axes per prompt rather than one from every axis. Empty strings are deliberate: they let an axis be absent, which is itself a variation worth sampling.
expression: shy, blush, closed mouth, looking away
axes.eye_effect_note: Empty weighted 3x -- her eyes are BLUE by identity and most frames should just show them. Symbol-shaped pupils recolour the iris, so they read as an expression effect for hyped/delighted, never as part of who she is.
axes.accessory_note: Empty weighted 3x. Headphones are an ACCESSORY here, not identity -- the reference art has none, and folding them into the identity block is one of the changes that produced the second Aria.
background: blurry background, depth of field, indoors
blurry background, depth of field, bokeh, monitor glow
axes.background_note: 'white background, simple background' is weighted 4x by repetition -- the avatar plate needs a flat white key so the page can multiply it against its own panel. BOTH tags are required together; tags.json records that 'simple background' alone still produces a gradient. Floating-star tags are deliberately ABSENT from this whole file: generated/aria_float_00001_.png reproduces the known_failure where 'floating stars, sparkle' overrides a white background into a purple starfield. Her stars live in the hair ornament, which renders fine on white.

negative.base: close-up, portrait, face focus, lowres, bad anatomy, bad hands, extra digits, fewer digits, text, error, cropped, worst quality, low quality, low score, bad score, average score, signature, watermark, username, blurry, greyscale, monochrome, multiple views, multiple girls, 2girls, long hair, twintails, blonde hair, cropped head, purple eyes, headphones, gradient hair, multicolored hair, blue hair, colored inner hair, blue shirt
negative.base_note: 'long hair, twintails, blonde hair' front-loaded per prompts.md -- hair drifting long is the most common failure. 'purple eyes, headphones' are negated because they are the signature tags of the OTHER Aria; without them the model drifts toward the aria_stars character, which is the exact split this file exists to prevent. face_lab.py removes a term from the negative automatically when the positive prompt asks for it. 'gradient hair, multicolored hair, blue hair, colored inner hair' and 'blue shirt' were added 2026-08-18 after the first 16 renders: her hair tips drifted blue and the shirt under the labcoat came out blue every time. The identity block is frozen, so per SKILL.md the correct lever for a recurring unwanted element is the negative, not a reworded positive. 'close-up, portrait, face focus' were front-loaded 2026-08-18 after the first framing choice produced macro crops: in Danbooru these are tight-head-shot tags, and suppressing them is what holds the bust framing. No positive framing in this file uses them, so there is no self-conflict -- and tune_negative() would withdraw them anyway if one ever did.
negative.portrait_add_note: tags.json, verified 2026-08-17: close-up framing invents a hand near the face unprompted. Dropped automatically when the prompt asks for hands (hand on own cheek, peace sign, v over eye, index finger raised, holding pen).

render.note: 832x1216 is the tall SDXL bucket; prompts.md requires tall for face work so the face sits high in the frame. cfg 5.0 / 28 steps / euler_ancestral is animagine-xl-4.0's measured setting from tags.json -- do NOT carry base SDXL's 7.5 over.

seeds.note: aria_clean and the LoRA dataset used 4242 and 770000; those are known to render this identity correctly, so the canon tier reuses them rather than gambling on fresh ones. The deep tier varies seeds freely because there the point is coverage, not consistency.

scene.note: Purple gamer-room scenes -- Ari's ask 2026-08-18, referenced to No Game No Life (Shiro's room: dark, lit almost entirely by monitor glow, violet dominant, screens stacked, cables everywhere). SEPARATE from the face tier on purpose: the avatar page multiplies her against its own panel, so a room behind her becomes a pasted-in rectangle. White stays for the avatar plate; these are for wallpapers, the control panel and the readme. Same frozen identity, so it is unmistakably her in both.
scene.measured: MEASURED 2026-08-18, seed 4242, generated/aria_scene_probe/. Seven readings rendered. The first four all came out BLUE despite 'purple theme' being in the prompt -- the model's default dark-room-with-monitors is blue-lit and the single tag loses to it. Weighting it up to (purple theme:1.4) alone (E) was still not enough. What worked (F) was BOTH piling on colour synonyms AND negating the competitor: 'blue theme, blue light, cyan' in the negative. G added rgb/led tags and drifted the star hair ornament orange, so the RGB vocabulary is left out.
